pages.text: Authentication Skip to content APIs Smartsheet API Brandfolder API Resource Management API AI & MCP Search Ctrl+K Smartsheet API Introduction Get started Guides Basics Authentication Base URL Dates and times HTTP and REST Pagination Pagination - SDK examples Resource access levels Sheets, rows, columns, and cells Query parameters Versioning and changes Advanced topics Best practices Reports Users Webhooks Updating code Limitations Deprecation process Additional resources Event types Webhook event types Error codes Changelog OpenAPI Reference Alternate Email addresses Attachments Automation Rules Cell Images Cells Columns Comments Contacts Cross-sheet References Dashboards Discussions Events Favorites Folders Governance Group Members Groups Home Imports Proofs Reports Rows Search Send via Email Server Info Sharing Sheet Summary Sheets Tokens Update Requests Users Webhooks Workspaces Schemas Guides / Basics Authentication Base URL Dates and times HTTP and REST Pagination Pagination - SDK examples Resource access levels Sheets, rows, columns, and cells Query parameters Versioning and changes / Authentication Last updated 9 months ago Authentication Copy Copy for LLM Copy page as Markdown for LLMs View as Markdown Open this page as Markdown Open in ChatGPT Get insights from ChatGPT Open in Claude Get insights from Claude Connect to Cursor Install MCP server on Cursor Connect to VS Code Install MCP server on VS Code The API authenticates using access tokens (API keys). You can generate access tokens in the Smartsheet UI. Important: Smartsheet Gov and Smartsheet Regions Europe use separate tokens from Smartsheet.com. Each API request requires passing in an access token as the Bearer value in your authorization header. For example, Authorization: Bearer JKlMNOpQ12RStUVwxYZAbcde3F5g6hijklM789 This article provides best practices to consider when working with the Smartsheet API and any access tokens (API keys), or other sensitive information. Authentication Approaches When choosing an authentication method, it is important to consider your integration scenario. Is the integration machine-to-machine without user interaction, or do you want user consent and interaction? If your scenario involves user consent and interaction, it's typically best to use OAuth with Smartsheet. Note that the Smartsheet implementation of OAuth 2.0 is a 3-legged process, which requires human intervention. See OAuth Walkthrough for details. If your scenario is strictly machine-to-machine, execute raw token requests over HTTPS. It's a straightforward, secure way to authenticate. See Access Token Best Practices for details. Each scenario requires an HTTP authorization header containing an access token. Note : In applications and for routine requests, it is best to use a shared account, such as ticket-processor@example.com, rather than your individual work account. Warning : If an unauthorized user gets a copy of this token, they will be able to access all Smartsheet data that you have access to, both to read and modify on your behalf. You should keep your tokens secure and do not share them with anyone. Access Token Best Practices You can generate access tokens in the Smartsheet UI. Never commit access tokens (API keys) to accessible version control systems like GitHub or BitBucket. Instead, use one of the following recommended storage options. Recommended Storage Options Use an app configuration tool suitable for deploying secrets to your app, or Use a config file outside of source control, or Use environment variables set outside of source control. If you have mistakenly deployed API keys to a publicly accessible location such as GitHub, then you should immediately revoke those API keys, revise your application to use a preferred method of key deployment, and then generate new keys. Storing in a database If you need to store API keys in a database, consider the following protections: Restrict access so API keys are only readable by the owner of the object Restrict read privileges to the database table Make sure your database or the disk the database is on is set to encrypt data at rest Note : When using any Smartsheet SDK, you can use the environment variable of SMARTSHEET_ACCESS_TOKEN . If the access token is null on input to the client builder, the SDK will automatically pick up the value of that environment variable. Revoking and Regenerating Tokens If you've committed code to a repository before implementing these security best practices, here are some steps to secure your API keys. For requests with raw tokens: Revoke the token Create a new token For OAuth with Smartsheet: Work through the OAuth Walkthrough to regenerate client secrets, auth codes, and tokens. Was this helpful? pages.title: Brandfolder API introduction
pages.text: Brandfolder API introduction Skip to content APIs Smartsheet API Brandfolder API Resource Management API AI & MCP Search Ctrl+K Brandfolder API Introduction Guides Insights Data Connector Error codes Changelog API Reference Assets Attachments Binary upload Brandfolders Collections Custom fields Invitations Labels Organizations Sections Tags User permissions Webhooks Schemas Last updated 1 year ago Brandfolder API introduction Copy Copy for LLM Copy page as Markdown for LLMs View as Markdown Open this page as Markdown Open in ChatGPT Get insights from ChatGPT Open in Claude Get insights from Claude Connect to Cursor Install MCP server on Cursor Connect to VS Code Install MCP server on VS Code The Brandfolder API enables you to programatically access and manage your organization's Brandfolder resources. By activating or using the Brandfolder API, you acknowledge and agree to the API License Agreement found here . V4 is a RESTful JSON API giving you programmatic access to the same resources you can access as a user of our website. You're probably wondering, "Which resources are those?" Well, each one has its own section in this documentation where you can learn in more detail exactly what operations you can perform in relation to that particular resource, but a bit of an overview here might be helpful. As a Brandfolder user, you are part of one or more Organizations . Organizations can have multiple Brandfolders . Brandfolders have Sections which hold Assets . Assets can also belong to multiple Collections within a Brandfolder . Assets have Attachments and can also have Tags and Custom Fields . You can also send Invitations to grant users access to Organizations , Brandfolders , and Collections . Authentication Authentication is performed with every API call by sending a header with your unique Brandfolder API key. Find your API key at https://brandfolder.com/profile#integrations . Click the icon to the right of your key to copy it to your clipboard. Use the key in your code when making requests to our API. The required header in each request is: Authorization: Bearer {BF_API_KEY} Each response to your API calls will only include the resources that you (or the User whose API key your application is using) can access based on your permissions. Making Requests All V4 requests are made via the following URL: https://brandfolder.com/api/v4 + resource endpoint When using our examples in your code, you'll need to make sure to replace {organization_id} (or any other resource ID like {asset_id} ) with the actual ID for the desired resource. For example, Fetch an Organization shows the endpoint as GET /organizations/{organization_id} . If you wish to fetch information about an Organization with an ID of plqlkk-22rw6g-3dqgx0 , then this means you need to make an HTTP request with a method of GET to https://brandfolder.com/api/v4/organizations/plqlkk-22rw6g-3dqgx0 We list parameters for each API endpoint. Query parameters describes some common query parameters. If our API responds to your request with an error, please see Error codes to understand what may have gone wrong. Was this helpful? pages.text: Resource Management API introduction Skip to content APIs Smartsheet API Brandfolder API Resource Management API AI & MCP Search Ctrl+K Resource Management API Introduction Getting started Guides Maintenance and Lifecycle Error codes Changelog OpenAPI reference API tokens Approvals Assignables Assignments Assignments per project Assignments per user Assignments with subtasks Availabilities Bill rates Budget item categories Budget items Custom fields Custom field values per project Custom field values per user Disciplines Expense items Holidays Leave types Phases Placeholder resources Project members Project memberships Projects Reports API Roles Status options Subtasks Tags per project Tags per user Time entries User status Users Users per project Webhooks Schemas Last updated 4 months ago Resource Management API introduction Copy Copy for LLM Copy page as Markdown for LLMs View as Markdown Open this page as Markdown Open in ChatGPT Get insights from ChatGPT Open in Claude Get insights from Claude Connect to Cursor Install MCP server on Cursor Connect to VS Code Install MCP server on VS Code The Resource Management API provides programmatic access to projects, user assignments, and more. The API implements standard HTTP REST operations that you can call to create, read, update, and delete Resource Management resources. Requirements: API access is only available on Pro , Enterprise , and Business Resource Management plans. If you're on a Trial plan, you can contact Support to request access. Base URL The Resource Management API server differs by region and product. Resource Management United States (US): https://api.rm.smartsheet.com/api/v1/ Resource Management Europe (EU): https://api.rm.smartsheet.eu/api/v1/ Resource Management Australia (AU): https://api.rm.smartsheet.au/api/v1/ Resource Management Gov: https://app.smartsheetgov.com/2.0/rm/api/v1 Authentication The API uses tokens (API keys) to authenticate requests. The following cURL command demonstrates retrieving a list of accessible projects: curl -X GET https://api.rm.smartsheet.com/api/v1/projects \ -H "auth: RM_API_TOKEN" The last line submits an API token as authorization credentials in an HTTP header named auth . You would replace RM_API_TOKEN with your API token. For information on accessing your organization's access token and making calls to Resource Management in the Gov product or in other geographic regions, refer to the Authentication article. What's next? Getting started (recommended) explains the fundamentals of using the API. OpenAPI reference lists operations and objects by resource, and provides a Try it interface to execute operations from right from within this site. Was this helpful? pages.title: Smartsheet MCP server introduction
pages.text: Smartsheet MCP server introduction Skip to content APIs Smartsheet API Brandfolder API Resource Management API AI & MCP Search Ctrl+K AI & MCP Introduction Quickstart Install the MCP server CLI Agent Power Tools MCP server tools MCP server toolsets Load server-side skills Changelog Last updated 4 weeks ago Smartsheet MCP server introduction Copy Copy for LLM Copy page as Markdown for LLMs View as Markdown Open this page as Markdown Open in ChatGPT Get insights from ChatGPT Open in Claude Get insights from Claude Connect to Cursor Install MCP server on Cursor Connect to VS Code Install MCP server on VS Code Interact with your project data in Smartsheet using the Smartsheet MCP server connected to Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI clients. Once connected, you can use natural language to read, analyze, and manage Smartsheet data to complement how you make decisions and get work done. Required plan: Business, Enterprise, or Advanced Work Management 🚀 What's new! MCP Connectors for ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Gemini Enterprise Plus, and Amazon Quick: Work with your Smartsheet projects in ChatGPT , Microsoft 365 Copilot (plus configuration video ), Gemini Enterprise Plus , and Amazon Quick . CLI Agent Power Tools available!: Use these open-source sub-agents locally to scan for bottlenecks and risks, clone project sheets, reassign tasks, and prepare for stand-ups and status communication. Check out the CLI Agent Power Tools overview . Automated workflow management tools: Create, enable/disable, and list your sheet workflow automations. Learn more at Automated workflows . Scenario planning tools: Experiment with project plan variations, mitigate risks, and increase project velocity right from within you favorite AI assistant. Refer to Scenario planning for details. Plan management tools: List a user's plans, query user seat usage and activity, and get license usage snapshots for plans. Check out the details at User plans . Portfolio tools: Create and manage portfolios, including templates and projects. Learn more at Portfolios . Ready to dive in? Start here Our Quickstart walks you through connecting the Smartsheet MCP server as an interactive companion in Claude Code. (These connection principles work across MCP-compatible AI clients.) Why use the MCP server? The Smartsheet MCP server bridges the gap between Smartsheet and AI models, allowing you to: Access Smartsheet data in real time Apply AI reasoning with Smartsheet's project and data management features Integrate with popular AI platforms including ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Gemini Enterprise Plus, or custom AI clients. Automate complex tasks that require both data analysis and decision-making Instead of manually copying data into an AI or writing custom API integrations, you can connect Smartsheet to AI clients to query projects, transform data, and trigger actions. How it works The MCP server exposes Smartsheet capabilities as tools that AI models can invoke. When you integrate Smartsheet with an AI client: The AI client can access (with your consent) predefined tools to summarize sheets, create rows, update data, and more. The client determines which tools are needed to solve your requests. The MCP server executes the request and returns structured data. The AI client processes the results and provides a response. This enables natural interactions like: "Show me all overdue tasks from the Marketing sheet and create a summary report" or "Update all project statuses based on the latest timeline changes." Getting started Dive into the following articles to connect your AI clients to the MCP server and familiarize yourself with the server's tools. Quickstart walks you through connecting the Smartsheet MCP server as an interactive companion in Claude Code. Query sheet structure, examine data patterns, and gather the information you need to write effective API code for sheet updates. (These connection principles work across MCP-compatible AI clients.) Install the Smartsheet MCP server has step-by-step instructions for connecting the Smartsheet MCP server to an AI client you use. Create a workspace with AI demonstrates creating a populated workspace based on the description of the work you're doing. Smartsheet MCP prompt library provides over one hundred example prompts, including prompts for onboarding to projects, detecting risks, auditing data, and comparing scenarios. For a deeper dive into the MCP server capabilities, check out Smartsheet MCP server tools . Was this helpful? Quickstart Next page On this page 🚀 What's new! Why use the MCP server? pages.title: Get Started
pages.text: Get Started Skip to content APIs Smartsheet API Brandfolder API Resource Management API AI & MCP Search Ctrl+K Smartsheet API Introduction Get started Guides Event types Webhook event types Error codes Changelog OpenAPI Reference Alternate Email addresses Attachments Automation Rules Cell Images Cells Columns Comments Contacts Cross-sheet References Dashboards Discussions Events Favorites Folders Governance Group Members Groups Home Imports Proofs Reports Rows Search Send via Email Server Info Sharing Sheet Summary Sheets Tokens Update Requests Users Webhooks Workspaces Schemas Last updated 3 months ago Get Started Copy Copy for LLM Copy page as Markdown for LLMs View as Markdown Open this page as Markdown Open in ChatGPT Get insights from ChatGPT Open in Claude Get insights from Claude Connect to Cursor Install MCP server on Cursor Connect to VS Code Install MCP server on VS Code Making your first API call is as easy as generating an API access token and sending a request to one of our API endpoints. If you prefer a visual walkthrough, watch this short (3-minute) video: To follow along with the step-by-step technical details , continue with the guide below. Generate an API access token Required plan: Business, Enterprise, or Advanced Work Management Generate an API access token in the Smartsheet UI. Go to the Smartsheet UI. Select your Account icon in the lower-left corner of the screen, and then select Personal Settings . The Personal Settings page for your account appears. Select the API Access tab. Click the Generate new access token button to generate an API access token. Note your access token and store it in a secure location. See Access Token Best Practices . Note: Tokens generated for Smartsheet, Smartsheet Regions instances, and Smartsheet Gov use the above generation process. However, these tokens aren't interchangeable. A token generated on Smartsheet doesn't work on a Smartsheet Regions instance or Smartsheet Gov. Each environment requires a token specifically generated for it. Call an API endpoint operation You can call an operation right from within this documentation site. Navigate to the page of an operation you want to call. For example, go to the List workspaces page. Click the Try it button, under the example request code on the right side of the operation page. A request editor appears. Apply your API access token in the Security tab by selecting the Bearer Token value field and then selecting Set value to start replacing the current value. In the Query tab, set or unset the operation's query parameters. When you're ready to call the operation, click the Send button. A response appears in the Response tab, at the bottom left of the editor window. You called the operation and received a response! You can call other Smartsheet operations the same way, from within the Smartsheet API documentation site. What's next? Use the API natively in a language supported by the Smartsheet SDKs: Python SDK Java SDK C# SDK JavaScript SDK Browse the REST API operations . Learn the basics , including authorization, HTTP & Rest, and more. Was this helpful?
